bio: In the southernmost town of Burgundy, this unassuming house in a pedestrian street is home to a benchmark of local gastronomy. The traditional architecture (bare beams and stonework and an old fireplace) is enhanced by contemporary details. Since 1991, Christian Gaulin has been celebrating the classical union of regional produce and modern techniques. Whenever he can, this solid technician sings a subtle ode to Bresse and Burgundy. Foodies can decadently indulge in frogs’ legs ravioli with garlic cream, tender pigeon, the breast roasted on the crown, the thigh confit with shallots, Charolais beef tournedos with pan-fried foie gras and a top-notch Grand Marnier soufflé. A believer in fine produce before all else, the chef cooks what he likes to eat – to our delight!...
